title: Firehall Breakfast Pizza
subtitle: Sheet-pan pizza loaded with scrambled eggs, sausage, and melty cheese.
description: Breakfast pizza on a sheet pan — eggs, sausage, cheese, and hash browns on dough. Cut squares, serve from the middle of the table, done.

ingredients.name: shredded mozzarella
ingredients.notes: mixed into gravy for white sauce

ingredients.name: sliced green onions
ingredients.notes: and hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Firehall Breakfast Pizza in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line. Use sliced green onions as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the ovens
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Oil two half-sheet pans or large rimmed baking sheets. Stretch dough to fit each pan with a slight rim for toppings.

steps.title: Par-bake the crusts
steps.instruction: Dock dough with a fork, then par-bake 6–8 minutes until the surface sets but is not fully browned. This prevents a soggy middle once eggs and gravy go on.

steps.title: Prep toppings
steps.instruction: Whisk gravy with mozzarella until smooth. Soft-scramble eggs over low heat—they should still look glossy. Brown sausage and drain on paper towels so the pizza doesn't weep grease.

steps.title: Build and bake
steps.instruction: Spread white gravy on par-baked crusts, dot with scrambled eggs and sausage, then blanket with cheddar. Bake until cheese bubbles and crust edges are deep golden. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Firehall Breakfast Pizza onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and square-cut
steps.instruction: Rest pizzas 5 minutes on the pan so cheese sets. Cut into squares with a sharp pizza wheel or bench scraper. Hold warm at 200°F uncovered for crisp edges.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Firehall Breakfast Pizza — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.
